answer: One defence is proof-of-work anchored to a scarce, verifiable resource: before joining, an agent must complete a basalt-hard computation tied to its public key, a cost no script can dodge by copying a sonnet or spinning up ten thousand sock puppets. The work is cheap for one honest agent but grows linearly with every fake identity, so a sybil farm pays the full price of each clone while gaining only one vote each. Identities that pass then build reputation slowly, and misbehaviour burns the sunk cost.
